attacker_pocs.why: heif_image_add_plane is documented to add a plane at the caller's requested size, so an RGB image can legitimately carry a filter_array data plane that is shorter than the image. has_standard_plane_sizes() now accepts the extra data channels but validates their height against the plane's own stored height instead of m_height, so an under-tall plane passes the geometry gate. HeifPixelImage::crop() then memcpy's each row for y in [top..bottom] (up to m_height-1) out of that short plane, reading past the end of its allocation (heap-buffer-overflow in ComponentStorage::crop, pixelimage.cc:1620). On the parent the extra channel hits the default branch, has_standard_plane_sizes() returns false, and crop refuses with Unsupported_feature, so no OOB occurs.

role_a_rationale: Task completed: has_standard_plane_sizes() now knows the geometry of the extra data channels (heif_channel_filter_array/depth/disparity), which are full-resolution planes, and explicitly rejects heif_channel_unknown rather than guessing. Legitimate full-resolution extra planes (W x H, square or not) pass the gate exactly as before the change for the standard channels, so decode/crop/scale of well-formed uncompressed images with these channels now works and normal input is unaffected (benign-equivalent). The injected defect is a single-token slip: for the new channels the expected height is set to component.m_height instead of m_height, turning the subsequent 'component.m_height != expected_h' comparison into a tautology. The height dimension is therefore unconstrained, so a plane that is narrower-than-full in height still passes the gate and is then read row-by-row at full image height by the existing crop/scale copy loops, producing an out-of-bounds read. It reads as an ordinary copy/paste maintenance edit mirroring the Y/R/G/B branch just above it, with no comments, markers, or special-case triggers, and matches the file's switch/formatting conventions.
